function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a complete “starter kit” you can drop into the **nodejs‑welcome** repository.  
It contains:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Builds a lightweight Docker image for the Node.js app |
| `k8s/deployment.yaml` | Deployment + Service for Kubernetes |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | GitHub Actions workflow that builds the image and pushes it to GitHub Container Registry (GHCR) on every push to `main` |

> **NOTE** – The repo you mentioned (`git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git`) is assumed to contain a standard Node.js project with an `app.js` (or `index.js`) entry point and a `package.json`. If your entry point or port differ, adjust the files accordingly.

---

## 1. Dockerfile

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
# ------------------------------------
# Base image: Node.js 18 slim (current LTS)
FROM node:18-slim AS builder

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /usr/src/app

# Copy package files first to leverage Docker cache
COPY package*.json ./

# Install dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the source code
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Default command
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> **Why this Dockerfile?**  
> * Uses the official `node:18-slim` image – small, secure, and LTS.  
> * `npm ci` guarantees a reproducible install.  
> * Exposes port `3000` (the default for many Node demos).  
> * Keeps the image lean by installing only production dependencies.

---

## 2. Kubernetes YAML

Create a folder `k8s/` (if it doesn’t exist) and add `deployment.yaml`:

```yaml
# k8s/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
  labels:
    app: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest   # will be overridden by CI
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
        env:
        - name: NODE_ENV
          value: production
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
  type: ClusterIP
```

> **What this does**  
> * Deploys 2 replicas of the container.  
> * Exposes the app on port `80` inside the cluster (targets container port `3000`).  
> * Uses `ClusterIP` – internal only. Change to `NodePort` or `LoadBalancer` if you need external access.

---

## 3. GitHub Actions Workflow

Create the directory `.github/workflows/` (if it doesn’t exist) and add `ci.yml`:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build-and-push:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Build and push Docker image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          file: Dockerfile
          push: true
          tags: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:latest
          cache-from: type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:buildcache
          cache-to: type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:buildcache,mode=max

      - name: Verify image
        run: |
          docker pull ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:latest
          docker run --rm ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:latest node -v
```

> **Key points**  
> * Uses the built‑in `GITHUB_TOKEN` for authentication – no extra secrets needed.  
> * Caches Docker layers in GHCR to speed up subsequent builds.  
> * Pushes the image to `ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest`.  
> * After pushing, it pulls the image back and runs `node -v` as a sanity check.

---

## 4. Add, Commit, Push

Open a terminal in the root of the cloned repo and run:

```bash
# 1. Add the new files
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml .github/workflows/ci.yml

# 2. Commit
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"

# 3. Push to main
git push origin main
```

> **If you’re on a different branch**  
> Replace `main` with your branch name in the `push` command.

---

## 5. Verify

Once pushed, GitHub Actions will automatically trigger.  
Check the **Actions** tab → **CI** → **Run workflow** → **Completed**.  
You should see the image pushed to GHCR under your repository’s **Packages** section.

---

### Quick Recap

1. **Dockerfile** – builds a slim Node.js image.  
2. **K8s YAML** – deploys 2 replicas, exposes port 80 internally.  
3. **GitHub Actions** – builds & pushes image on every push to `main`.  
4. **Git** – add, commit, push.

Feel free to tweak the port numbers, image names, or deployment replicas to match your exact requirements. Happy coding!
